title: Don Byas, Paul Bascomb and Tab Smith
summary: They try to place Don Byas and Paul Bascomb in the 1940-42 band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: When -- well did -- Lester never did come back, did he?
Yes, he did. He came --
When did he come back?
Didn't -- he came back after the war for a little while, didn't he? I feel pretty sure of it. But, you know something -- somebody was in that band we've missed was Don Byas
Yeah. Don't you have --
Well, my eye just went over it. See, Tab Smith was in that band in 1940.
Right. Right. Right. Which was a good band. Well, Don Byas was there during that time Tab was there wasn't he?
Yeah. Oh. But then in 1942 he had Paul Bascomb on tenor. How long was he with the band?
Paul Bascomb?
Yes. Bud Ted Bascomb's brother.
I know who he is, but I've forgotten all about him.
(laugh).
He's a good tenor player.
I know. Isn't that something, I've --
You've forgotten that he was ever in the band?
Yeah. Who was in the band with him?

1940 -- Ed Lewis, Al Killian, Harry Edison, Buck Clayton, Vic Dickenson, Dicky Wells, Dan Minor, Earl Warren, Tab Smith, Buddy Tate, Paul Bascomb. And, you know -- you've got Jo Jones and Walter Page there. And, then it's -- Don Byas is at the beginning of 1941.
Yeah. Well, then Bascomb didn't stay in there very long, then. He was just --
No. Not according to this.
No. He wasn't there long for anybody to remember. I'd forgotten all about him.
Mm. Stanley, when you're reading off those personnels which you're reading off very fast and very soft --
Yeah.
-- that may not, you know, be that clear.
Well, I missed this period. You see, Don Byas was there for about a couple of years.
Mm hmm. Mm hmm.
Well, I mean, you know, he after all, is playing the same kind of thing that -- Lucky Thompson and Paul Gonsalves did. You know, he's the sort of contrast --
Yeah. Yeah. They were. They were very close -- Don Byas and Lucky.
Yeah.
Friends, you mean?
As far as --
Style?
As far as style is concerned.
Yeah. Well, and is Buddy there all through?
Yeah. Buddy's there all that time.
Yeah. He's permanent on clarinet, you know -- after Herschel left.

Yeah. Yeah. Well, what I'd like to know, Stan, is in '46 when the rhythm section goes back to the original rhythm section -- you know -- let's not jump to '50 yet. I mean, in those four years are there all that many changes -- after the war is finished -- after it's no longer a question of people being drafted -- are there still all those changes occuring all the time in those four years?
Not quite as rapidly, but -- no. That's holding -- the personnel is holding pretty much the same.
Well, that's interesting, isn't it? Because, it shows, you know, that the war caused all those changes.
Right.
